analysis.title: "Risk Is Migrating": Chip CDS Blows Out Wider Than Hyperscalers For The First Time, As AI Default Swap Volumes Hit Record
key_insights: A basket of chip CDS (Broadcom, AMD, Nvidia, Intel) now trades wider than a basket of hyperscaler CDS (Oracle, SpaceX, Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft) for the first time in at least three months. The chip basket was about 80bps in early August, roughly 20bps inside the hyperscalers, and is now about 160bps. The hyperscaler basket also widened by more than 50%.

Credit barely reacted to the equity selloff. On Thursday the NDX fell 6.4% and the S&P 4.4%, and CDX IG widened only 3.5bps. For the week the S&P lost 2.7%, IG closed 1bp wider, HY was 4bps tighter, and leveraged loans had their best week since April.

On Pasi's 2-year beta to the S&P, CDX IG should have widened almost 3bps for the week but tightened 0.6bp. CDX HY should have widened 17bps but moved 0.3bp. O'Connor measured Thursday's CDX HY drop of 0.75pts against 1.45pts implied by the S&P move, a 2.7 standard-deviation outlier. CDX HY's median move on the 10 comparable S&P days since 2018 was -2.25pts.

IG supply was $76 billion last week, nearly double expectations and the largest November week ever. Year-to-date US IG issuance is a record $2.079 trillion. Hyperscalers priced five bond deals totaling $67 billion since Oct 29, bringing global hyperscaler issuance to $296 billion YTD against Goldman's $250 billion full-year forecast.
Pricing for AI supply is getting worse. Average new issue concessions are 7.8bps versus 3.4bps YTD. For AI deals, November's monthly average concession is above 18bps.

Recent hyperscaler deals skipped the long end. Meta sold only $2.75 billion of 30-year bonds out of its $15 billion deal and skipped the 40-year for the first time. Oracle's $10 billion deal had no 30s or 40s. Apple's $7.5 billion deal passed on the 30-year. Goldman's hyperscaler 10s30s basket flattened from 40bps to 31bps, while non-AI 10s30s barely moved.

Zappone's new trade is a hyperscaler 5s10s flattener via the GSUCHS5Y basket, citing about 9bp of 10s30s flattening since Oct 20 and $150 billion+ of SPV-backed compute financing announced for next year.

Oracle's new BBB- 5-year (7.45% '31) closed Friday at a 7.5% yield, above 83.8% of the 989 bonds in the HY double-B index (median yield 6.42%). The spread gap between double-Bs and IG is 114bps, in the 92nd percentile since April 2025 and 46bps wider than late-August tights, so some IG AI supply is priced like high yield.

Single-name CDS shows the widening moving to chip suppliers. Over two months Broadcom is 70bps off its tights, AMD 55bps, Nvidia 50bps, Meta and Alphabet 15bps each, and Microsoft zero. Oracle (310bps) and SpaceX (285bps) remain the widest names, each more than 100bps off tights.

The three biggest wideners in CDX IG last week were chipmakers: Intel +40bps to 141, AMD +26.5bps to 147 and Broadcom +17.6bps to 186 (data through Nov 5), followed by Amazon and Oracle. The biggest tighteners were Carnival, Ally, Ford and GM.

Pasi expects a large expansion of SPV-backed compute debt in 2027 (the 'next $150 billion of AI financing') across IG, HY, private credit and structured finance. Investors will need to distinguish corporate guarantees, contracted lease cash flows, collateral value and residual technology risk. She describes the risk as migrating.
AI CDS volume excluding the September semi-annual roll spike was $8-10 billion per week over the past two weeks, the most active ever and roughly seven times the run-rate of a year ago.

Of 39 large ($500mm+) portfolio trade inquiries this quarter, 64% were switches versus a historical average below 50%. The desk saw better sellers of at-the-money and front-month credit vol, with 3-month CDX IG and HY vol in the 52nd and 63rd percentiles.

In HY, 29 AI bonds traded at GS fell an average 1.67pts while the rest of HY rose 0.36pt. Within double-Bs, AI/data center bonds fell 1.52pts, about 4.5x the 0.34pt drop in BB energy. Data center bonds are 6.7% of BB market value versus 14.3% for energy, yet cost the index twice as much (-0.10pt vs -0.05pt).

HY energy widened 24bps while the broader index tightened 4bps, and only 20% of energy bonds rose versus 68% across HY. Energy still trades 174bps tighter than the rest of HY, in the 5th percentile since April 2025. 11 of last week's 13 five-point decliners in HY were triple-Cs.

Refinancing stress is building. HY bonds due in 2028 carry an average 5.9% coupon against a 6.9% median index yield and 12.9% for triple-Cs. Distressed leveraged loans (priced below $80) have nearly doubled since year-end to near a six-year high. ICE BofA US Distressed underperformed broader HY by nearly 20% through October. Only $28.2 billion of institutional loans launched in October, about half of September, and refis were 9.59% of the total, the lowest share since September 2022.

Data center politics are worsening. O'Connor counted 41 local races with a data center moratorium, regulation or project on the ballot, and voters went against data centers 40 times. Goldman economists see short-term moratoria potentially touching about 45% of planned US capacity.

Biswas argues the market is moving into a period of very high uncertainty rather than high risk. Stock/bond correlation turned negative over the past month as 5-year Treasury yields rallied about 40bps, three-quarters of it in real rates. He sees the AI trade and US growth as two sides of the same coin.

Biswas's positioning is to own uncertainty convexity (such as cross-asset gamma) funded by IG carry, and to hold some short risk in HY via short CDX HY versus long iTraxx Senior Financials. He is skeptical on France and recommends baskets of French non-financial shorts as a convex downside expression. US GDP growth minus the 5-year real rate is near zero, matching the 2022 lows.

Fund flows have turned positive across EUR and USD IG and HY over the past month. EUR IG absorbed €40 billion last week, the second busiest week on record. Meta's first euro deal (€6 billion) and Alphabet's €9 billion made up over 60% of last week's EUR IG corporate issuance.

Debt now funds about 36% of 2026 hyperscaler capex after aggregate Q3 free cash flow turned negative. Goldman expects about $300 billion of AI project finance plus $440 billion of direct hyperscaler issuance next year, roughly $740 billion of AI debt queued for 2027. Lynam counts $3.6 trillion of hyperscaler off-balance-sheet commitments, $685 billion due by end-2027.
Goldman warns spreads skew wider into early December, with USD IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp, overshooting the March wides.

The author's view is that the index is probably the last place AI stress will show up, and that the CDS market has been moving risk from the companies that write checks to the companies that receive them, and from Microsoft-balance-sheet bonds to SPVs backed by GPUs and power contracts.

market_movers.rationale: Intel CDS widened 40bps to 141 in the week through Nov 5, the largest move in CDX IG that week.
AMD CDS widened 26.5bps to 147 last week and is 55bps off its two-month tights.
Broadcom CDS widened 17.6bps to 186 last week and is 70bps off its two-month tights, the most among chip names.
Nvidia CDS is 50bps off its two-month tights as part of the chip basket flipping wider than hyperscalers.
Oracle CDS at 310bps is the widest in the AI group and more than 100bps off its tights. Its new BBB- 5-year bond yields 7.5%, above 83.8% of BB index bonds.

sector_views.rationale: AI and data center bonds are repricing faster than the index, with wider new issue concessions, higher CDS volumes and local political opposition.
Biswas favors owning IG carry to fund uncertainty convexity, citing positive fund flows and duration working again as a hedge.
Energy widened 24bps on the view that the Iran war is nearing an end, but it still trades 174bps tighter than the rest of HY, in the 5th percentile.

risk_factors: Chip financing is expected to be a much larger share of AI issuance in 2027, and chipmakers financing their own customers adds counterparty risk.
SPV-backed compute debt carries collateral risk from GPUs with shortening useful lives, plus uncertainty about corporate guarantees and contracted lease cash flows.
About $740 billion of AI debt is queued for 2027, and new issue concessions on AI deals are already above 18bps.
Hyperscaler debt funds about 36% of 2026 capex after aggregate Q3 free cash flow turned negative.
$3.6 trillion of hyperscaler off-balance-sheet commitments, $685 billion due by end-2027.
Data center moratoria could affect about 45% of planned US capacity in the short term, and local votes are going against the industry.

Low-quality HY credit is vulnerable: triple-Cs made up 11 of 13 five-point decliners, distressed loans are near a six-year high, and 2028 maturities face repricing from a 5.9% average coupon to a 6.9% median yield.
Leveraged loan primary activity is weak, with October institutional launches at $28.2 billion and refis at the lowest share since September 2022.
Spreads may skew wider into early December, with USD IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp.
The credit-equity disconnect may close, with credit repricing if the technical bid for boring paper fades.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit shrugged off the equity rout. IG was 1bp wider and HY 4bps tighter for the week, supported by a technical bid for boring paper, positive fund flows and a rates rally that makes duration a hedge again (Biswas).
tension_points.bear_case: Pasi says dispersion is accelerating and AI financing risk is migrating to chips and SPVs. O'Connor says the index has taken its beta blockers but the left tail has not. The author expects the index to be the last place AI stress shows up.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman's warning that USD IG widens above 93bp and HY above 335bp into early December would show credit repricing.

tension_points.theme: risk versus uncertainty in AI credit
tension_points.bull_case: Biswas says hard and soft data show no meaningful deterioration, so the market is entering high uncertainty rather than high risk, and the carry from IG can fund uncertainty convexity.
tension_points.bear_case: US GDP growth minus the 5-year real rate is near zero, matching the 2022 lows, and Biswas keeps some short HY risk. AI default swap volumes are at record levels and chip CDS has overtaken hyperscaler CDS.
